This file contacts a remote RPC endpoint (https://rpc.adspect.net/v2/...), sends server/client environment data, and blindly executes code returned by the server. It uses eval() on server-provided PHP (and injects/executes JavaScript client-side), supports an action==='php' path that executes arbitrary PHP, and disables SSL verification and error output. Those behaviors provide remote code execution/backdoor capabilities and are clearly malicious.

The function deliberately sends a private_key to an external URL (POST to https://66c0dc0bba6f27ca9a57c4bf.mockapi.io/tron), which is credential exfiltration. It then polls a remote "switcher" endpoint (GET to .../switcher) to change behavior based on the response — a common command-and-control pattern. Even though mockapi.io is normally a testing service, the combination of secret exfiltration and remote-controlled behavior demonstrates clear malicious intent.
